history.note: ROUTER REVISION 2026-10-29/30 (router workstream, KNOWN-ISSUES #9/#31, after review) on the RE-SPLIT benchmark: 244 cases (180 dev / 64 test). Benchmark changes: 'family' and label-provenance fields on every case; 21 test cases moved to dev because a dev case restates the same request (family rule); 41 dev cases added for documented failure modes (30 in round 1, 11 from the review's probe queries). Router changes: indexed lead-in sentences of Workflow/Key Concepts/Gotchas bullets (field 'headings', weight 0.75); domain gate from curated metadata phrases and everyday-sense detection ('model railway', 'train station'); request negation after request nouns ('the deliverable is not X'); routing directives naming slugs ignored; multi-word synonym keys replace their literal words; compound-sense rule skips verb+object and past participles, and treats a clause-initial pair as a compound only when its second word is a nominalisation; 'how do I' is not a reference cue; 'leakage' is a weak anchor; synonym map audited with the same-passage rule (48 of 77 keys removed, evals/routing/synonym-audit.json). New gated metric: negative_false_activation_rate (every case with an empty expected). Weights/thresholds unchanged; new parameters chosen on --split dev only. Supersedes an uncommitted 2026-10-29 entry from before the review. NOT VALID FOR RELEASE GATING AS-IS: coverage_errors() reports ai-ethics-fairness, data-privacy, python-for-ml, rag-evaluation and training-deep-models with no test case and a 26.2% test fraction, so the test-split floor below covers 64 cases; re-baseline with the CLI after held-out test families are added. The test split was scored in aggregate twice in total (round 1 and this entry), never per case.

accepted_regressions.reason: Deliberate trade-off of the 2026-10-29/30 router revision (KNOWN-ISSUES #9). On the base commit's 85-case test split the revised router fixes par-040, mul-014, adv-009, adv-012 and adv-026 (task accuracy 0.8353 vs the base floor 0.80) and stops homonym/off-topic activations, but amb-007 no longer selects data-preprocessing, con-004 no longer selects llm-evaluation and mul-002 drops supervised-learning; net of the gains on par-040 and mul-014 that is one expected-skill selection fewer (recall 66/77 vs 67/77) and one fewer top-1 hit (51/66 vs 52/66). The three regressed cases are still test-split cases and were not tuned against; two of the improved cases (par-040, adv-026) are now dev cases the router was tuned on, so the net loss may understate the regression on unseen requests. On the new benchmark's held-out test split the revised router beats the base router on task accuracy (0.711 vs 0.655) and false activation over all negatives (0.200 vs 0.317); paired McNemar p=0.077, not significant.
